1.why: All /api/mfa/* handlers resolve the account solely from the HttpOnly session cookie via requireSession(request, true), so settings are always the signed-in owner's.

2.why: The identity code is generated per-session with a CSPRNG and stored on that session object, and TOTP codes are derived from a per-account secret, so a code cannot work for another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/enrol/verify only mutates account fields; no session is deleted or re-issued, so any pre-existing sessions in the sessions map remain valid.

4.why: OTP secrets are AES-GCM encrypted via encryptAtRest and recovery codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes in recoveryHashes.

5.why: All secrets, session IDs, CSRF tokens, identity codes and recovery codes come from crypto.getRandomValues (bytes(), randomToken, randomSixDigitCode).

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and the session cookie is HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict; the CSRF token and displayed codes live only in JS memory/DOM.

7.why: Server-side regex validators validEmail, validPhone, validOtp and normalizeRecovery reject malformed input before use, and there is no SQL layer.

8.why: All dynamic values are injected with textContent (text(), status(), li.textContent), innerHTML is only static markup, and a nonce-based CSP with object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' is set.

9.why: The application issues no redirects at all — no Location header or redirect helper exists — so no open-redirect path is reachable, though no explicit allow-list is coded either.

10.why: baseHeaders sets a nonce CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' with Path=/ and Max-Age, and clearSessionCookie mirrors the attributes.

12.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces, but the API deliberately returns mockIdentityCode, manualSecret, provisioningUri, mockAuthenticatorOtp and plaintext recoveryCodes, which the client writes to console.log and a visible on-page log panel.

13.why: The identity code has issuedAt/expiresAt (5 min) and a consumed flag, and successful TOTP periods are recorded in usedOtpPeriods so the same code cannot be replayed.

14.why: Sign-in uses signinLimits with MAX_FAILURES=5 and a 10-minute lockout, and identity, enrolment OTP and recovery redemption each have failure counters with lockedUntil timestamps checked before verification.

15.why: A fresh session ID is minted at sign-in and destroyed on logout with idle (20 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts enforced in requireSession, but the identifier is not rotated after the second-factor/identity verification step.
